213839392.review:
Solidly crafted, relaxing, and very charming.

This is a modest yet very clever Sokoban-style puzzle game, with an inviting minimalist presentation, fun music, and a good dose of comedy at its heart.

Basically, you have words that function as physical objects and can be pushed around to create phrases that, in turn, establish and modify the properties of other objects in the world.

The simplest example is right in the title.

"Baba is You" (three movable words) establishes that "Baba", that white thing, is you, the player, and therefore is controlled by your commands. 

So... If you replace the word "Baba" with something else, say, the word "Wall," suddenly, the visible walls in the game world become you.

Yes, you become the wall and start walking with it.

Let's say you create the phrase "Wall is Baba". All the walls transform into the white thing.

The words have specific properties, and the goal is to rearrange them to fulfill the victory condition, which usually consists of reaching a specific object, which can be anything.

"Wall is Stop" means that walls cannot be crossed. Therefore, breaking the sentence allows you to cross the walls.

"Flag is Win" means that you need to reach the flag to win the level. Therefore, placing the word "Win" in a sentence containing another object makes that object the objective.

"Wall is Win" means that touching any wall will win the level.

And so on.

Breaking "Baba is You," without an immediate replacement that conditions the "You," essentially severs your control and ability to interact, promptly reinforced by the white noise of death that triggers as soon as you make that mistake.

The fun lies precisely in the mental and comical twists that the game's solutions offer. It's so good.

As you progress, new rules, words, and variables are added. Objects with multiple functions, using the same word to build more than one sentence, using words to push things, etc.

Correcting mistakes is extremely easy. You can undo one move at a time or restart the entire level with the press of a button.

The puzzles also have a open-ended nature, giving you the freedom to find your own solutions, instead of being stuck with just one correct answer.

They really managed to explore the enormous potential contained in such a simple idea. It's an instantly intuitive and very cozy game with a good amount of content.

I'm still amazed at how fresh and innovative the Sokoban iterations can be, even after so many years.

Definitely recommend it.

Baba Is You - a name-based breakdown

[b]Baba[/b]
Word, noun. Name of the fluffy little bunny creature you control.
Don't get too attached, though, as their quantity - and even existance - is in a state of constant flux.
One wrong move may eradicate them all or lead to an unstoppable chain of self-duplication that will only stop once the entire universe is filled with nothing but Baba.
You may understand the inner machinations of Baba, but you cannot truly comprehend them.

[b]Is[/b]
Word, verb. Sounds innocent enough, but under the wrong circumstances it may tear apart the very fabric of the universe itself is contained in, so beware.
Many of creatures and objects have been brought into existence by it. It, however, cares not for any of them and may end their existence at any time it pleases.
Nor does it care about anything's state of being. It may choose to transmute anything into something else at a whim, without any consideration of the consciousness it bestows and rips away.

[b]You[/b]
Word, descriptor. The illusion of control in the palm of your hand. Invade the minds of innocent beings to further your own goals, careless to whatever happens to them now or after you discard them.
Possess inanimate objects, move them about, and haunt every creature around in view. They perceive but do not understand. Unable to flee, they may only fear.
However, this also applies to you. Without power over anything, you too become powerless. Unable to reassert control yourself, you are forced to wait out the heat death of this doomed universe. 
You locate the cosmic reset button. You hope that it may change your fate. You are unsure if it truly reset everything, including you, or just created a different timeline at the beginning of time while preserving all the old ones.

ARE YOU BABA OR IS BABA YOU?

Вкратце: хорошая головоломка, но удовольствие она приносит только при повторном прохождении. 

[hr][/hr]
40% уровней (по моему ощущению): 1) не дают четкую цель, 2) требуют глубокое понимание, как именно блоки правил взаимодействуют друг с другом. При первом прохождении ты не знаешь эту информацию, поэтому приходится отсекать десятки возможных вариантов, пока не найдешь тот, что задумал разработчик. Брутфорс не поможет: уровни защищены от случайного перебора — надо именно вдумываться в то, что ты делаешь.

Иногда это работает. Мой любимый уровень [i]Automated Doors[/i] я проходил несколько дней, и когда методом исключения нашёл единственно возможное решение, затем проверил его и оно оказалось верным — меня чуть не разорвало от счастья. Но гораздо чаще подобные уровни просто раздражали и проходить их не хотелось.

Есть объективно плохие уровни:
[olist]
[*] [i]Insulation[/i], [i]Guardians[/i] и [i]The Return of Scenic Pond[/i] — содержат отвлекающие элементы (red herring). В головоломках такое считается дурным тоном.
[*] [i]Tectonic Movements[/i] — решение видно сразу, но последовательность действий можно подобрать только долгим брутфорсом.
[*] [i]The Box[/i] — мета-гиммик с конченой логикой правил, до которой невозможно додуматься. 
[/olist]
И это даже не весь список.

Первые два прохождения я дропнул. На третьем зашёл далеко, но всё-равно задолбался и сначала стал смотртеть подсказки, а потом и полные решения в интернете. Даже финальный уровень решить сам не смог. 
И только спустя пять лет, когда я забыл все решения, но примерно помню цели и правила, прохождение наконец стало приятным.

Правда, теперь я ненавижу новые паки уровней, потому что хочу пройти их без подсказок, но тоже намертво в них застрял)))

206418051.review:
(I'm writing this at 3 am out of boredom)

This is a game I've been playing on and off since mid 2023. Do I recommend it? Absolutely. BUT only to a specific type of person: someone who can tolerate one of the most bs difficulty curves in any video game, and still find enjoyment (a masochist). The game starts out innocently enough. Push this rock, create this rule, touch the flag etc. At its core this is what the game is about. However once you reach world 5ish, the game starts throwing some very complicated rules at you. "Shift" in particular which is used in some of the most complicated solutions in the game. The difficulty then peaks (IMO) at world 7, which introduces the first instance of text stacking AKA the mechanic that made me want to bash my head into a wall on multiple occasions. Did I say the difficulty peaks at world 7? Because I lied. There is not 1, not 2, NOT 3, but FOUR secret worlds after the world map. At this point, you will begin to understand that everything you did up until that point was just the tutorial. These 4 secret worlds contain the most mind bending and abstract puzzles I've ever seen. Two of these puzzles which took me 5 hours to beat, and I consider myself to be pretty good at puzzle games.

If you just want a relaxing puzzle game to play, skip any level you spend more than 10 mins on. But if you're a masochist like me, welcome to the game you've been searching for. Enjoy 60-80 hours of hell.

Only half joking. The game IS extremely difficult, but it is also insanely well designed, and I rarely felt that the puzzles were too unfair or cryptic. Even on the hardest puzzles, I left thinking "That actually made a lot of sense". Don't feel too bad if you spent a while on a puzzle that was pretty simple (I've done this a few times). The game conditions you to think abstractly even when it isn't necessary, which will lead to that happening. 

Honestly, I was going to write a lot more, but I dont want to spoil TOO much. If you are a puzzle enthusiast or enjoy challenging games, this is a must experience. The final world may be my favorite sequence of levels in any video game. Overall I would rate this a 10/10, and it quickly became one of my favorite games of all time upon completion. But as I said earlier, it definitely isn't for everyone so keep that in mind.

Here are my favorite levels from the game:

"Queue"
"Meteor Strike"
"Heavy Cloud"
"Automated Doors"
"Baba Has Keke"
"The Box"
"Parade"

Thank you for listening to my yap session.

Super fun and difficult puzzle game, almost every puzzle has one "Ah ha!" moment. A lot of negative reviews are straight up false. 
I heard one say the game doesn't teach how the rules work properly, even though it's one of the aspects I feel the game does the best at. A lot of puzzles focus on breaking assumptions you made about certain rules/objects, one instance being the very start of the game [spoiler] , that level being level 7, Grassyard. [/spoiler].
 Another one I heard was that the game was too strict and that most levels had only one solution. This really doesn't make sense to me. Of course there's one solution! It's a PUZZLE game. If you have an "open-ended" puzzle game, it simply won't work out. The levels would be too easy, the "Aha!" moment wouldn't be there, and the game wouldn't really be able to teach you anything.
 Yet another negative review I saw was that there were too many "redherrings." First off all, there's only a slim few red herrings in the game, and secondly, those red herrings often end up teaching you something about how the puzzle/rules works. Take the level Changeless, where often [spoiler] players form the sentence, "Rock Is Flag," however, the doesn't work due to the sentence, "Rock Is Rock". [/spoiler]
There's a couple of negative reviews that are completely valid though. The game's steep difficulty curve and a lack of a built in hint system can definitely be a turnoff for some people, especially the latter. If you're playing this game and need a hint, I recommend you use the site "Baba Is Hint", as it never spoils a solution. 
In summary, if you like hard games, play Baba Is You. If you don't like hard games, try it out for a little.

204674512.review:
I'm not sure I would call it bad, but I will say I don't recommend it, because I think the praise it's gotten is too extreme, so it doesn't need more recommendation. What it needs is for people to hear the downsides and reasons you might not want to play.

Yes, I know I've become the meme of the guy who plays for 200 hours but leaves a negative review. In my defense, the in-game timers say it's more like 150 hours. Much better.

I think the positives are clear from the trailer, the concept is great, and the presentation is very charming.

The negative comes down to the way the game's progression is structured. Here's the structure I wanted:
A concept is introduced in a simple way, then built upon in subsequent levels, ratcheting up the challenge and complexity consistently over time until it reaches a satisfying climax. Then the game says "Mission Accomplished!" and you’re done. Then there are even harder bonus levels for the hardcore players. Ideally, this structure would be present in individual areas and in the whole game. Within each level, the process of solving it would also be a slow climax as you work out multiple ideas that have to be put together.

Here's the structure I don't want:
A concept is not introduced. The challenge of a level is realizing the concept. Once you realize the concept, the level is easy and you solve it, but beforehand, it seems impossible. It's not a process of putting together multiple pieces, it's just about realizing one thing. Then once you've realized the thing, it's not built upon in future levels; it either appears again the same way, or it doesn't appear again. The levels don't ratchet up in difficulty and complexity consistently as the game progresses, rather it's a grab-bag of levels with wildly different difficulties, some way harder than others in the same area. You don’t get a climax and then get told you’re done, rather there’s an anti-climax as each area usually requires only a few levels out of the total to be completed, so you feel incomplete and unsatisfied even as you’re told you can move on now. But if you take this incompleteness as a challenge to get 100%, you will be punished for this decision as other levels in the same area will be so hard that getting 100% will only be fun for hardcore players.

I’m not going to say this game’s structure is none of type 1 and all of type 2, but there’s way more type 2 than I would have liked, and way too little type 1.

The second type of structure won’t be bad for everyone, I just wish I had known that was what the game was going to be when I started. It’s not optimized for you to get into a flow state where you feel consistently challenged, it’s optimized for you to feel stuck until there’s an AHA moment at which point you’re basically done. Some of these AHA moments are great, maybe the best thing about the game is its sense of humor, but I didn’t feel like I was being guided towards the AHA much of the time. It would have been more fun to be shown the level by someone else than to actually solve it.

This is compounded by the fact that certain mechanics are ambiguous or unintuitive in how they work. Some things trigger at the beginning of a move, some at the end, and there’s no visual indicator of which, you just have to guess which it is and memorize once you find out. Some combos of words can be put together, others can’t, and it’s normally sensical but sometimes arbitrary. Some words don’t work how you would expect. The AHA isn’t even necessarily something you could deduce from the start, you have to test if it works. To be fair, the process of testing can be fun in itself, but it’s also time consuming and punishing with how fiddly it feels to do anything in this game, so I wish I had been rewarded for that work by getting to understand an elegant logical system where everything makes sense. It doesn’t feel like that, a lot of it feels arbitrary. This also means it’s easy to forget the details of how things work and have to re-test.

Youtuber Patricia Taxxon has talked about how she distinguishes between “puzzle games” and “riddle games.” Puzzle games reward understanding the basic logical mechanics, while riddle games reward guessing what the designer meant. That made me think of Baba Is You. It’s not true that it’s a riddle game and not a puzzle game, but it has more of the former than I wanted, and that’s what it felt like to play much of the time.

The criticisms in this review clearly weren’t enough to stop me from playing the game a LOT, so it’s not like I was never having fun. But a lot of the time playing it felt more like a compulsion, unfinished business I wanted to resolve more than something I found true meaning in. My own tendency to compulsively do things I don’t actually enjoy is my own flaw of course, I just feel like the game enabled it by being so unsatisfying, while constantly feeling like it could have been so much more satisfying. The game isn’t bad, but I believe the narrative that it’s a masterpiece is bad because it makes it sound like you should put more time into it and expect more out of it than it can really deliver. I think the developer came up with a genius concept for a game, and maybe it was so good that they got a bit carried away in terms of scope and the overall structure suffered. Or maybe this disjointed minefield of secrets is exactly what they wanted to create and my expectations for the game were set incorrectly.

(Youtuber Matthewmatosis said that Hempuli’s previous game Environmental Station Alpha also had an unsatisfying conclusion, with a very hard optional challenge after that which people might feel obligated to do - even though it’s not fun for them - because the game’s ending didn’t feel conclusive. I haven’t played that game, so I don’t know if that’s true, but it reminds me of my experience with Baba Is You.)

It’s possible I’m simply stupid or mentally ill in a way that is incompatible with loving this game, and that’s not the game’s fault. However, I’m writing this review so others like me can have more info about what the game is like and avoid my fate. Also, with a smoother difficulty curve, it would be easier to start, enjoy the stuff that’s on my level, and stop when it gets too frustrating, rather than being constantly tempted by easy levels and then hit in the face when the next level requires thinking a word means something that was never established.

	Are you a Smart Person Who Enjoys Feeling Dumb When You're Not? Then this Is the Game for You.
	I’m a former programmer. I love symbolic logic. I’m a big fan of Human Resource Machine and 7 Billion Humans—not just logic puzzles, but games that are explicitly about computer programming, dressed up in visual metaphors. Those games are programming exercises disguised as puzzles—and I loved them.
	Baba Is You shares a lot of that DNA. It’s not as directly tied to programming concepts, but the core idea—rewriting rules and manipulating symbolic logic to solve problems—lives in the same space. So let’s be clear: this game wasn’t too abstract for me. It wasn’t confusing (at first). I was ready for it, and I loved the concept.
	And for the first couple of hours, it lives up to that promise. The aesthetic is charming. The early puzzles make you feel clever. The systems are clean and tight. You think: “I’ve found something special.”
	Then it all falls apart.
	The difficulty curve goes off a cliff, but not in a way that feels smart or earned. The game introduces new words and mechanics with almost no internal tutorialization. You’re just thrown into a level with a new piece of logic and expected to deduce its behavior by trial and error.
	Early on, learning new rules and behaviors feels rewarding. Before long, it becomes opaque. Ultimately, it’s just exhausting.
	As you progress, the logic gets fiddly, inconsistent, and sometimes indecipherable. Some puzzles hinge on behaviors that don’t quite line up with how similar elements have worked before. I found myself watching walkthroughs and still not fully understanding why a solution worked. Not because I didn’t grasp the rules, but because the rules weren’t explained, and the feedback loop wasn’t clear.
	Eventually, the game becomes more about interpreting layers of meta-logic than solving actual puzzles. It stops being about manipulating rules to achieve a goal and starts being about manipulating the game itself (left vague to avoid spoilers). I’d read solutions, perform the steps, and still be left thinking, “How in the world could anyone arrive at that via rational thought, as opposed to brute force trial-and-error?” Even with a walkthrough, I couldn’t always internalize what the puzzle was asking. That’s not a satisfying challenge—it’s a disconnect between the game and the player.
	And yes, I’ll say it: a lot of people praising this game aren’t being totally honest. Either about how often they looked up solutions, or how frustrating and not-fun the experience actually became over time. There’s a prestige that comes with finishing a game like this. But prestige isn’t the same as enjoyment. And it’s certainly not a good reason to recommend the game as “fun and clever” to players who may not realize what they’re getting into.
	Baba Is You is a brilliant concept, inconsistently executed. I admire the ambition. I admire the design. I just didn’t have fun. And if you’re the kind of person who normally thrives on logic games and systems puzzles, you might be surprised by just how fast this one turns from joy into fatigue.
	Another very reluctant thumbs down for me. There so much greatness here, but prospective players really should understand what they're getting themselves into with this Black Box of a game tied with a Moebius Strip bow.

202681812.review:
I'll join the unfortunately limited chorus of negative review on this one; because there does need to be some more honesty about this games' flaws.  

First, to cover what other negative reviews say:
* I have to agree that puzzles are very narrow, with only a limited number of ways to solve them. 
* on the other hand, I do NOT agree that there is an issue with mechanics being too obtuse or poorly explained - part of the concept includes experimenting with combinations of words to see what happens. 
Neither of the above is the root of what makes the game so damn frustrating, however.

 The real issue is that most of the time the game isn't about the rules & logic aspect, but rather stupid fiddly positioning challenges of pushing things around just-so.

For example - 1 of the current levels I'm stuck on requires pushing an object A over to an object B to unlock the win condition. Object A is also affected by gravity, & if I let it fall too far I simply can't recover it. I have down pat how I need to change the rules around - I know I need to borrow a spare IS in order to hold object A. I know I later need to re-use that same IS to re-open the win condition. I have the logic changes down pat, so I should just be able to solve it, right?
Wrong - because I need to do a bunch of fiddly counting & careful positioning of my 2 Babas so they can push object A without dropping it, & also be able to move back to change the rules later to enable the win condition. And it is very clear the designer deliberately added additional gaps to make the pushing & positioning a little extra tricky. I'm not thinking right now about how to change the rules, I'm thinking about how to place 1 Baba so he can catch the falling object from the other Baba without making me restart or rewind.

And that is where most of the difficulty in most of the puzzles comes from: counting precise # moves left/right & being careful not to push words into positions where you can't revert them. Fiddly, fiddly block-pushing puzzles with no lee-way for making mistakes; emphasized much more than the logic/rules based aspect promoted in the description & previews.

This review is based primarily on the base game, and not the mods or the new adventure pack which I'm positive I'll play sometime down the line.

Learning is something I consider beautiful. A seemingly simple idea can expand into countless complex ideas, and seeing it happen slowly over time is something beautiful. However, the things that we learn have been found only after centuries and millenia, and with how many things there are in the world, you simply cannot learn everything that has been discovered.  Instead of exploring the world you already know, how about an entirely new world, much more simplified, yet still as complex as you want it to be?

This game revels in you learning its' mechanics. There are very few written tutorials, as you are often left to your own to figure out how it works. It does typically lead you in the right direction, but occasionally there's moments that may feel a bit unfair for some. The farther you go along, the more you realise the truth of the world and its mechanisms, yet the difficulty only escalates.

If you are willing to spend the time to learn a new world, and even spend up to hours on some of the most grueling puzzles, then this game is for you. If you are willing to receive some hints towards the (or a) correct solution, then consider using https://www.keyofw.com/baba-is-hint. It's not perfect, as it spoils a bit more than I would have liked and is a bit outdated, but worth checking out if you feel absolutely stuck with no clue what to do. Consider waiting a day while thinking about it, and maybe you'll figure something out.

このゲームは「自分でパズルのルールを改変させる」というパズルゲームとしては斬新極まりない内容のゲームです。

ステージ上にルールを構成するための単語が配置されており、プレイヤーはBABAとなってその単語を組み合わせてステージを攻略していくのですが、なんとプレイヤーが操作する対象をBABAから別のものに改変することができます。ゴールに設定してある物体を変えることができます。何ならプレイヤーが操作する対象そのものをゴールに設定することさえあります。
ステージごとにある程度はできることが限られてはいますが、それでもステージをクリアするためにルールを改変していくのです。
そのため一つのステージに複数の解放が存在することもあり、できることの自由度があまりにも高すぎるのです。

[h2] Короткая версия: [/h2] 

Если нравятся пазл-игры, это одно из лучших предложений на рынке, дальше только играть и наслаждаться. ИМХО эта игра идеальна для телефона/планшета/СД, на ПК тяжело идут сессии дольше 1 часа, единственное отличие, что моды только на ПК идут, а они довольно интересные для любителей экстрима.

[h2] Длинная версия: [/h2] 

Игра делится на 3 части:

[b] Первая часть. [/b]  Это оригинальная игра с [spoiler] 231 [/spoiler]  уровнем, ту нас знакомят с базой и разными вариациями как этой базой пользоваться, под конец немного экстрима.
Умный пазл дизайн и правильно выстроенная кривая сложности дарят реально веселый геймплей. Автор тот еще тролль и очень часто пользуется приемом, когда пускает вас по ложному следу, то есть вы заходите на уровень, все выглядит так, что задача будет решаться как-то так, и уже под самый конец, радостно идя к финишу выясняется, что еще с самого начала ты шел не в том направлении, кто хоть раз пробовал создавать пазлы знает как это непросто. 

Еще один плюс это многослойность задач, мало того, что нужно понять как будут взаимодействовать механики, чтобы задачу вообще можно было решить, так еще и все расставить и переместить надо так, чтобы работало, например в одной из самых сложных задач базовой игры FURTHER FIELDS, догадаться, что должно быть сделано, 5-10 минут, реализация 30+. Бывает часто такое, что разгадав новую особенность механики и радостно идя до финиша, обнаруживается, что ты не знаешь как до него дойти потому то надо понять еще одну новую особенность механики, это реально круто. 

Ах да, с этого надо было начинать, мне больше всего игра понравилась тем, что тебя тут никто не водит за ручку, никто тебе не будет объяснять что и как работает, начинаешь чувствоать себя ученым-испытателем, выдвигаешь гипотезу, ставишь опыты, делаешь выводы, имплементируешь, не раз было такое, что я давно понял как решать уровень, но очень хотелось попробовать другие комбинации и что они делают. Это офигеть какой интересный пазл геймплей.

Ну и вишенка на торте, уже из вышесказанного понятно, что игра наполнена интересными задачами, которые требуют оригинального подхода к решениям, НО автор сверху добавил гениальный класс задач “extra”, которые требуют зачастую реально мыслить нестандартно или буквально выйти за пределы коробки, это мои любимые задачи и я с них словил огромный кайф. Отдельно хочется отметить задачу THE FLOATIEST PALTFORMS, это гениальный пример когда задача идеально сбалансирована во всем, восторг.

Еще немного про многослойность, автор буквально ее добавил везде, не спешите с выводами о том как выглядит игровой мир, я неспроста добавил спойлер на количество задач, их тут больше чем кажется, что отдельный вид кайфа для любителей шоу “Тачка на прокачку”, [spoiler] мы добавили тебе уровень внутри уровня, чтобы ты смог решить там еще один уровень внутри уровня, ЛАЙК! [/spoiler]

[b] Вторая часть. [/b] еще одно гениальное решение, автор сделал МУЗЕЙ в виде задач, (их разумеется надо будет все решить), которые он забраковал или которые не прошли финальную проверку или которые были в последствии улучшены или которые тестеры попросили не добавлять, я бы реально задушился на SWAP+TELE, также добавил свои комментарии, чем он руководствовался, что понравилось, а что нет, это же просто офигенно! Огромный лайк за идею и реализацию и отдельный лайк за уровень TRAIN, красивая идея, но игровое поле и вправду плохо читается.

[b] Третья часть. [/b] Тут поговорю о том, что не понравилось и так сложилось, что последний пак уровней часто этим страдал. Как я упоминал выше, решить задачу на уровне концепции не равно добежать до победного флажка, иногда игра требует до безумия педантично точного перемещения игрового персонажа и блоков, одна клетка влево и даже при правильных условиях ты не сможешь добежать до финиша, также привет задачам на MORE, где надо планировать каждый шаг, и вот ты уже решаешь не пазлы, а сидишь занимаешься подбором и перебором вариантов, это очень унылый геймплей и лично для меня нет никакой разницы с тем, чтобы зайти порешать задачи типа “найди мат в N ходов”, является ли это пазл контентом..наверное да, весело ли в это играть, точно нет. Третья часть игры в большинстве своем предлагает как раз задачи на просчет вариантов, прямо душно играть было, были конечно и гемы, например BABA IS EMPTY как глоток свежего воздуха, но в целом было желание дропнуть, пару раз надо было даже понять как работает движок игры и в какой последовательности срабатывают условия, которые активируются в один ход. Наверное уровни типа FLIGHT ACADEMY, это граница, которую не стоит переступать. В общем не зашел мне этот пак, кроме последнего острова, там уже больше развлекательный контент, хоть немного подышать дали.

[h2] Сложность. [/h2] 
Не хочется лезть в оценку сложности, но своих 5 копеек вставлю. Много натыкался на отзывы, что игру невозможно пройти без подсказок или что это доступно лишь для единиц и тд, я не согласен с тем, что игра ОЧЕНЬ сложная, все зависит от того сколько времени на уровень вы готовы потратить, были задачи где я проводил 1-3+ часов, но таких я вспомню от силы 15-20, остальное это 10-20 минут, иногда по 30-60, итого на все уровни без подсказок ушло около 150 часов, в среднем 20 минут на задачу, думаю это средний показатель, дальше уже сами судите, является ли это показателем сложности, учитывая, что львиная доля времени уходит на эксперименты и знакомство с механиками. Конечно, если нет желания тратить на некоторые задачи больше часа, тогда да, очень сложно. Другое дело, что у игры огромный потенциал быть очень сложной, я начал играть мод ALPHABABA, после задач оттуда, классическая БАБА кажется вступительным экзаменом, что на самом деле круто, ведь и любители задач попроще и посложнее найдут себе контент по душе, что для меня показатель хорошей игры.

[h2] Вывод [/h2]  очевиден, пробуйте, играйте, продукт реально качественный, мне было очень весело и интересно.

201551564.review:
Baba is You is likely to be one of the most brilliant and intuitively-based games that I have ever played.  This is also arguably the most frustrating game I have ever played in my life, and I am glad to have played it and am now done with it.  I have played this game on three computers over the last 5 years, and the experience is one I will never forget.

Baba is You, Baba is me, Baba is whatever you want Baba to be.  The limits are boundless.  Much like how the English language only follows rules in very specific instances, so does this game.  You can make up your own rules, as long as the game allows it.  Baba is Level, Baba is No.  The rules are mere lines of code that can be manipulated to be whatever you want.  
The first few worlds were actually pretty fun and pretty interesting to play around with.  Many of them I could figure out with *relative* ease.  But the further in, and deeper in, you go, the harder and more nonsensical the game becomes.  You can become the game itself, and as long as the rule works with the game, you quite literally can do what you want.  I will admit, I did resort to a guide for much of the later levels past World 10, but I am sure if I spent endless hours playing this game, I too could have *eventually* figured it out.  I have so much respect for those few players that had stuck with this game for however long it took to individually figure out each level and gather all the achievements for that is no easy feat.  Without their guidance, I would not be able to do the same.  

The music is very calm and makes it cozy, though sometimes it did make it hard for me to focus.  But I did love the variety in it.  I was perpetually haunted by the fact that every mistake ending in the need to restart a level was accompanied by the absence of music and nothing but hollow wind.  As such, I tried to complete the level with as few mistakes as possible to avoid it.  Otherwise, all the music was fairly pleasant.

I will say that this game does have achievements, most of which increase in difficulty the further into the game you go.  As of the time of writing this, roughly 54% of people that have played the game finished the Water is Sink achievement, roughly 27% finished the Cog is Push achievement, roughly 20% finished the Box has Key achievement, roughly 14% finished the Leaf is Move achievement, and less than 10% have gotten any of the 14 other achievements.  The tags of this game do state that it is a difficult logic and puzzle game, and this game presents as such.  Do not be fooled, it is *incredibly* invigorating and rewarding to get those achievements, but those statistics cannot be ignored.  This is not a game to achievement hunt lightly.  To do so is a labor of love and you must have incredible time and patience.  

There are very few games I have encountered that enable you to interact in the game itself in the way Baba is You does.  Sure, there are games that remember your choices, but in my humble opinion, this is still unmatched in the way you can play with the meta and coding of this game to get what you want.  This game is not for everybody.  This is not a cozy puzzle game.  It is fun and novel, but it is also frustrating and rewarding.  I do think this game is 10/10, but play at your risk and know what you are getting into, but you truly will not know until you start up the game.

200438113.review: Baba Is You is a puzzle game where you manipulate the rules of the puzzle to solve the puzzle. It's like a programming language. Take C++. When you start progressing, you learn different constructs and techniques to accomplish your goal. When you run into a problem, you can run and debug test cases to try and get your chunk of code to work. But, if you go in too deep, aka the post-game, you run into a roadblock which needs to be solved with abstraction. At that point, C++ only becomes one of the tools, and now you're focusing on source libraries which your code manipulates (or vice versa) to solve your task. I could have looked up documentation to figure out how to implement the source library, which in this case is manipulating the overworld to manipulate the level to manipulate the overworld to progress. But I already had loads of fun learning the game and solving these problems, and then the game needing me to overlap objects broke my brain for a bit.

199538373.review:
Baba Is You is a brilliantly inventive puzzle game that challenges players to think outside the box and manipulate rules within the game world to solve increasingly complex challenges. From the moment you start playing, it becomes clear that this title defies traditional puzzle game conventions. The core mechanic revolves around a simple yet profound concept: the rules of the game are represented as movable words within the environment. By rearranging these words, players can alter the fundamental logic of the game—changing what objects are called, how they behave, or even what rules are in effect. This innovative approach creates a sandbox of possibility where players are encouraged to experiment and discover solutions through creative thinking rather than rote memorization or trial-and-error.

The game's visual style is minimalistic but charming, with a clean, pixel-art aesthetic that keeps the focus squarely on the puzzle mechanics. The simplicity of the visuals works in tandem with the gameplay, making it easier to identify and manipulate the rule objects and interactable elements within each level. The soundtrack and sound effects are unobtrusive but effective, providing subtle feedback that enhances the immersive experience without distracting from the core gameplay. The interface is intuitive, allowing players to pick up and experiment with the rule-changing mechanics quickly, which is essential given the game’s emphasis on rapid experimentation and iterative problem-solving.

What sets Baba Is You apart from other puzzle games is its depth and flexibility. Each level is essentially a puzzle of language, logic, and spatial reasoning. Players often find themselves rewriting the rules to turn obstacles into pathways or to make seemingly impossible objects behave in new ways. For instance, changing "Wall Is Stop" to "Wall Is You" allows the player to become the wall, or rewriting "Flag Is Win" to "Flag Is You" makes reaching the flag the primary goal, shifting the entire approach to a level. The game rewards out-of-the-box thinking, and many puzzles have multiple solutions, encouraging experimentation and exploration. This open-endedness fosters a sense of mastery and discovery that is both satisfying and addictive.

The difficulty curve is well-balanced, with early levels serving as gentle tutorials that introduce the core mechanics, gradually escalating to more abstract and challenging puzzles that require a deep understanding of the rule system. As players advance, they encounter increasingly intricate scenarios that demand multi-step solutions, combining different rule manipulations and spatial arrangements. The game also offers a sandbox mode for players to create and share their own puzzles, which has helped foster a vibrant community of puzzle enthusiasts. The level design is consistently clever, often subverting expectations and playing with logic in surprising ways. Baba Is You is a testament to how a simple concept, when executed with ingenuity and clarity, can produce a deeply engaging and intellectually rewarding experience. It’s a game that encourages perseverance, creativity, and flexible thinking, making it a standout title in the puzzle genre and a must-play for anyone who enjoys brain-teasing challenges.

Rating: 9/10

Look, i do recommend this game. On average, it's great. Although you are basically railroaded into solution, building the railroad takes a lot of trial and error. In most severe cases, the railroad is supposed to fly, or even have a crossroad, or layered, or exist outside of three-dimensional reality. 
90% of the time you don't have any blueprints or hints, so just like in real life, you have to painstakingly guess what the hell did client want from you. Again, on average, unraveling the solution is very fun and done in elegant way. However, there are always outliers that make you stuck for hours, until you finally give up and look for solution, only to just let out either a scream or a queit "oh, so you can do that. cool." 
Most of the rules and interactions between them make sense and are intuitive. Even some supposed "rule breaks" are understandable. But again, game doesn't want to share any additional info. Gameplay aside, both visuals and sounds are minimalistic, but really pleasant. Helps you relax a bit when you're stuck for an hour. 
So why do i recommend this game? Partially because, despite its immense difficulty and some shortcoming, i do aknowledge that it's well made and offers a great puzzle experience.

198559233.review:
a great puzzle game that just goes on too long and pushes itself too close to its limits.
it's obviously a game that's inspired greatly by programming languages; the way its IS operator works is more like the = operator in most coding languages than natural language; the game objects function like programming objects, with the action/property words acting like methods; levels function almost like coding challenges, where you are given a limited set of objects and methods and have to understand all the nuanced interactions between them in order to create a solution. this is a lot of fun but can get extremely frustrating when you're trying to figure out how a bunch of functions interact with each other  (and themselves) without being able to see the actual code of said functions. you'll go through extensive periods of "caveman banging rocks together" trying to figure this all out, but when you hit that spark and figure out how to use it, that's video games baybee. that being said, there's a reason real code is annotated and why we have resources like Stack Overflow: you do eventually get sick of banging rocks together without making progress. 

there's a few levels here and there that irk me (and which i had no shame in looking up after seeing what the solution was), and i wish it was maybe half as long and got to the good stuff earlier by cutting the filler levels. as it is, the game is just a bit too sprawling, a bit too recursive. i kept making breakthroughs only to be confronted with "oh there's yet another layer" and it felt like it was taking the piss eventually. by the end, all of the intended solutions felt like exploits and glitches, and my mindset eventually became "okay but how can i break this function to do something totally unintended". except it's not unintended, it's the only solution. the puzzles became a bit contrarian and silly, but were still incredibly satisfying to solve (when you aren't hopelessly stuck). 

the game feels like a celebration of spaghetti code, of coding without an IDE, of learning a new programming language by just bashing functions and operators together to see what happens. it's silly and cute, and devilishly difficult towards the end. it became a bit of a slog for me but still would heartily recommend!

Baba Is You est un chef-d'œuvre de puzzle, avec une idée brillante : manipuler les règles du jeu comme des blocs à pousser. Le concept est génial, et l’exécution, ultra précise.

Cela dit, ce n’est pas un jeu accessible à tous. La difficulté grimpe vite, et certaines énigmes peuvent vous bloquer pendant des jours, voire des semaines. Si vous aimez les casse-têtes vraiment coriaces, qui demandent de la persévérance, de la créativité et parfois même de revoir toute votre façon de penser, alors foncez. Vous en aurez pour votre argent, et plus encore.

En revanche, si vous êtes plutôt du genre à vous frustrer vite, ou à préférer des puzzles plus "linéaires", ce jeu risque de vous épuiser. Il ne vous prend jamais par la main, et il faut aimer se battre pour chaque victoire.

Bref : un bijou pour les passionnés de puzzles, mais à ne pas mettre entre toutes les mains.

197599185.review:
[h2]Are you a Smart Person Who Enjoys Feeling Dumb When You're Not?  Then this Is the Game for You.[/h2]

I’m a former programmer. I love symbolic logic. I’m a big fan of [i]Human Resource Machine[/i] and [i]7 Billion Humans[/i]—not just logic puzzles, but [b]games that are explicitly about computer programming[/b], dressed up in visual metaphors. Those games are programming exercises disguised as puzzles—and I loved them.

[i]Baba Is You[/i] shares a lot of that DNA. It’s not as directly tied to programming concepts, but the core idea—rewriting rules and manipulating symbolic logic to solve problems—lives in the same space. So let’s be clear: [b]this game wasn’t too abstract for me. It wasn’t confusing (at first).[/b] [b]I was ready for it, and I loved the concept.[/b]

And for the first couple of hours, it lives up to that promise. The aesthetic is charming. The early puzzles make you feel clever. The systems are clean and tight. You think: [i]“I’ve found something special.”[/i]

Then it all falls apart.

[b]The difficulty curve goes off a cliff[/b], but not in a way that feels smart or earned. The game introduces new words and mechanics with [b]almost no internal tutorialization[/b]. You’re just thrown into a level with a new piece of logic and expected to deduce its behavior by trial and error. 

Early on, learning new rules and behaviors feels rewarding. Before long, it becomes opaque.  Ultimately, it’s just exhausting.

As you progress, the logic gets [b]fiddly, inconsistent, and sometimes indecipherable[/b]. Some puzzles hinge on behaviors that don’t quite line up with how similar elements have worked before. I found myself watching walkthroughs and still not fully understanding why a solution worked. Not because I didn’t grasp the rules, but because the rules weren’t explained, and the feedback loop wasn’t clear.

[b]Eventually, the game becomes more about interpreting layers of meta-logic than solving actual puzzles.[/b] It stops being about manipulating rules to achieve a goal and starts being about [i]manipulating the game itself [/i] (left vague to avoid spoilers). I’d read solutions, perform the steps, and still be left thinking, [i]“How in the world could anyone arrive at that via rational thought, as opposed to brute force trial-and-error?”[/i] Even with a walkthrough, I couldn’t always internalize what the puzzle was asking. [b]That’s not a satisfying challenge—it’s a disconnect between the game and the player.[/b]

And yes, I’ll say it: [b]a lot of people praising this game aren’t being totally honest.[/b] Either about [i]how often they looked up solutions[/i], or [i]how frustrating and not-fun the experience actually became over time[/i]. There’s a prestige that comes with finishing a game like this. But prestige isn’t the same as enjoyment. [b]And it’s certainly not a good reason to recommend the game as “fun and clever” to players who may not realize what they’re getting into.[/b]

[b][i]Baba Is You[/i] is a brilliant concept, inconsistently executed.[/b] I admire the ambition. I admire the design. I just didn’t have fun. And if you’re the kind of person who normally thrives on logic games and systems puzzles, you might be surprised by just how fast this one turns from joy into fatigue.

Another very reluctant thumbs down for me.  There so much greatness here, but prospective players really should understand what they're getting themselves into with this Black Box of a game tied with a Moebius Strip bow.

196896415.review:
久闻Baba大名，今日推完果然精彩。

推的不是一般的箱子，而是“规则”箱。替换单词的同时也是在变换机制，改变 “主-谓-宾” 结构的句子语义就能创造出丰富可能。虽然在玩之前就已经对这种玩法有所耳闻，但自己开始真上手后也能感受到变换带来的新奇乐趣。
另外，谜题的解法不止于变换语义，还会经常考验玩家的一些“骚操作"。比如：特定情况下可以让操作的物品与文字重叠，有几关就需要利用这个技巧来破坏限制语句。还有譬如“文字叠叠乐”、“shift脚踩脚驱动”、“我是你 你是我 鬼畜循环”等...... 如果靠自己探索发现出这些神秘机制能带来很大惊喜，不过这也可能导致试错成本升高，不太容易能想到。

虽然有需要一些跳跃性思维，但大部分关卡的解法都能逻辑推理，有迹可循，不至于完全无从下手。baba的附加的变体关质量很高，狠狠打击惯性思维，相似布局的关卡有可能是完全不同的思路。总共231题，没有凑数的重复关卡，量大管饱。表关、附加关、隐藏关、meta关应有尽有。后期引入的 text 和 level 又让人眼前一亮。个人感觉最有意思的是“B A B A”系列的关（特别是 ABC-额外1），拆散字母后组合很大程度扩展了交叉性，解出来瞬间十分有乐趣与成就感。

另外baba也有关卡编辑器和许多社区自制的关卡，扩展性强，足够耐玩，感觉是买的最值的解谜游戏之一了。

Baba Is You is one of the most original puzzle games ever made. If you enjoy bending your brain and messing with logic instead of just button-mashing, this one is a gem. Each level is like a brain teaser where you have to rethink how the game works. Just be ready to sit there sometimes staring at “Flag is Win”… with no flag in sight.

I wouldn’t recommend Baba Is You to just anyone. It’s definitely not casual – it looks cute and simple, but it can be really frustrating. If you get stuck, the game doesn’t offer any hints or help. You either take a break and come back later with a fresh mind, or you’ll probably end up searching for the solution online.
This isn’t the kind of game you play to relax after a long day. It’s more like a brain gym – super clever, but also mentally exhausting at times.

196151219.review:
The game is great at the beginning but its extreme obtuseness and reliance on trial and error and long and exact sequences of moves in later levels leave it so the only end point it leads you to sooner or later is to eventually give up in frustration. 

If you are ok with looking up solutions, being entertained passively by being shown a solution that you never would have thought of, and enjoy "progressing" in that manner then it's fine, and this indeed is how the vast majority of people enjoy this game. You can see in the review playtimes that almost without exception people start playing, do a few of the easier levels, are delighted by the cleverness of the solutions, leave a thumbs up at that point, then never play again.

But if you are someone who refuses to look up a guide and tries to persist on solving it yourself then the game simply becomes just an infinite series of brick walls where you progress not by solving puzzles with an established set of rules, but by fumbling around and guessing what the rules even are.

In the end this is ironically a puzzle game that corners you into enjoying it passively by being shown solutions of mechanics which are hidden and unexplained, instead of allowing you to actually solve a puzzle by establishing its rules in a clear way beforehand. It's "cleverness through obscurity", and while a lot of people are entertained by that as evidenced by its review score, for me that makes it fundamentally a bad puzzle game.

194901367.review:
It's hard to believe that a sokoban game about changing the logic of its levels would appeal to a broad range of people. What caught your eye when you first saw "Baba Is You"?

    Take a look at any screenshot or video featuring the game and you will see short sentences and charming creatures, the combination of which create an accessible shorthand for relaying a puzzle. Once familiar with this shorthand, "Baba Is You" can also viewed as a collection of comic strips featuring recurring characters in amusing predicaments. This is imitated in the Steam reviews where people make up their own variations of the game's rules to share an experience or communicate an emotion.

    "Baba Is You" is a monumental achievement in game design; it is built on a concept that seems simple enough to prompt the occasional "I wish I came up with that", executed to an incredibly high standard. Each of the subworlds seen on the main map contains only a small selection of levels to avoid repetitive puzzles and maintain the desired difficulty. I cannot imagine the number of iterations it took to get these levels to be as streamlined and neat as they are. The difficulty increases quickly as you figure out the unique mechanics of the word blocks; the only hints you get come from the level names and the starting layout of the words and objects.

    Solutions to the puzzles are never immediately obvious and often lead to satisfying interactions or surprisingly funny moments (a good number of which come from trying out the obvious solutions). "Baba Is You" feeds both the feeling of accomplishment that comes from solving a hard puzzle and the enjoyment you get from applying the rules you learned to set off a fun chain reaction. The rewind feature is a lifesaver, allowing you to easily test an interaction without having to redo the previous parts of the level when your plan inevitably falls apart.

    The cherry on top is the inclusion of an easy to use level editor with a way to share or download levels online. Hempuli (the creator of "Baba Is You") released two official level packs that should contain enough levels to satisfy those brave enough to be asking for a sequel.

    The wonderful art style, ingenious level design an distinct regional music left a lasting impression; I'm truly excited to experience any games this developer may come up with.

193763659.review:
Some kind of wizard made Baba is You because I've never had to exercise so much lateral thinking. The difficulty progression is designed to make the player think of increasingly creative or obscure ways to make or apply the rules. This allows the puzzles to usually remain simple but still baffling. Figuring out new tricks lead to satisfying "eureka" moments that make the game so compelling.

The downside is I got stuck on quite a few puzzles for a long time. This happened frequently enough that trying to complete all the levels felt like a slog. However, the game seems to acknowledge its difficulty because it requires only about half or less of most area's levels be completed before another area is unlocked. Each new area introduces at least a couple new building blocks for constructing rules, so just progressing through the game doesn't feel so bad.

There are some pretty fun secrets to find too, but while these secrets are the game's most mind-blowing moments, they ultimately led me to finally get tired of the game as well. It's hard to explain without spoilers, but these secrets lead down a rabbit hole that I felt goes too deep. If you're the type who likes to complete everything in a game (without looking up a walkthrough, of course), be prepared for a long journey with this one.

[h2]Baba Is You And Game Is Phenomenal[/h2]

[i]Baba Is You[/i] is undoubtedly, one of the best logic puzzle games that money can buy.

The premise is so simple, yet so well executed. You control the world around you with blocks you can push, sort of like a [i]Sokoban[/i] style of puzzle, but so much deeper. You move blocks, some being the objects, like rocks, or baba, others being the property, like win or stop, finally, the connectors, like [i]is[/i] and [i]and[/i]. For example, a level could have a variety of objects and properties. If I were to make the sentence, "Wall Is Win", that would mean, touching any of the wall blocks in the level would cause me to beat the level. There's so much you can do with this mechanic, the possibilities are practically endless. 

There's more than 200 levels, with a lot of them telling some sort of story, with the title.

I love how the later levels are able to be broken down to reveal more secrets, almost like a 4th wall break, in a sense.

Don't get me started on the soundtrack, it's so retro, yet such an enjoyable listen.

I have nothing left to say except, get this game, it's so unique and a once in a lifetime puzzle game!

191527186.review:
[h1]Baba is Baba is Flag is Win[/h1]

[b][u]PROS[/u]:[/b]  Baba Is You is a fantastic & amazingly well put together word puzzle game.  The game relies on pushing words & items around to solve various puzzles.  These puzzles range from deceptively complex to strangely simple almost off & on.  Though the soundtrack is charming but fairly forgettable, the visuals are simple & adorable, accurately showing off what's expected in minimal detail.  Even better, the game comes with a level editor, & the various stages the fans have come up with shows the love the game has.

[b][u]CONS[/u]:[/b]  Unfortunately, the only real con of the game is rather than having a learning curve, this game has a beyond 90 degree learning cliff.  Some of the latter stages are quite difficult, as one should expect, but the majority of difficulty in the later areas is simply finding the stages.  Some overworlds are harder to navigate than the puzzles inside them.  Thankfully, the fanbase has written solutions on how to navigate, but for the difficulty to overhang like that is a feat in itself.

[b][u]ACHIEVEMENTS[/u]:[/b]  Like the title, this list is deceptively simple.  In order to clear out the list, one must complete all stages.  The issue is the game is incredibly vague on both where additional stages are & how to access them.  Though the stages can be difficult, they are still quite fun & can start to become simpler as one gets a handle on the game's mechanics & thinking outside a standard word puzzle.  The key to remember is everything in this game can break if the phrasing allows it.

[b][u]FINAL[/u]:[/b]  Baba Is You is an astounding puzzle game in just what it manages to accomplish.  Despite the stunning difficult in the latter quarter of the game, everything works in a way that feels satisfying to complete.  Still, the obnoxious hunt to find the stages & absolute free fall of difficulty makes it almost necessary to use a guide just to proceed, as the game does little to guide a player itself.  The difficulty will be a factor in those wanting to complete it, but for puzzle fans, this is a must own, at the very least for the brilliantly executed concept & gratifying brain teasers.

Talking back about the game, I just adored the game dynamics and innovative design: the combination of box pushing and coding snippets are fine tuned just too intricately in the game. Few games allow players to experiment everything possible and interact with every element in it in a logical and meaningful way, and I could only think of Breath of the Wild and Crypt of the Necrodancer besides Baba Is You. I also just love meta games that challenge every rule in the game, and Baba just did a perfect, and even layered, job in uncovering what rules can be perceived and utilized. When I looked at the images from the gallery, I had an immediate flashback to The Witness, where I sat there for hours watching those Easter videos. I'm posting this review when I'm still not very far into the game. 

Compared to some of the other puzzle games I have played, this one feels like one of the harder ones. However, that's hard for be to be certain about, since a lot of the other puzzle games I've played are 3D-puzzle-platformers (Portal, Antichamber, etc.)

Compared to those, Baba Is You is a different beast entirely. So far, it's puzzles essentially revolve around mixing logic, almost like programming logic, with physical 2D-placement of puzzle elements. 

Essentially, where other puzzle games I have played might require you to, say, start by doing X to retrieve Y to do Z, Baba Is You would ask you to start by doing X, set Y to A, and now time it such that Z is done without setting A to 'DELETE'. 

It's been a hard game for me to get used to. It has definitely hit me with moments where I'm thinking, "...What is this nonsense? I don't have the tools here for that?! HOW IS THAT EVEN- oh that's what I had to do....HOW WAS I SUPPOSED TO FIGURE THAT OUT?!"

If you're looking for a puzzle game that can absolutely force you to think, you found it. I have quite a ways to go, and I'm nervous about what's left. The other nice thing is that it's very much a pick-up/put-down kind of game - so far I've just been pulling it up, cracking a few puzzles, then putting it down to play another game or just do something else.

Overall, I'd say I'm having fun with it. Just try not to let it get to you, and don't feel bad about just dropping it for a little while if it leaves you scrambling to come up with solutions to some of the levels.

I've REALLY liked the first half or so if the game, and made myself to play through the second half for the sake of completion. The puzzles are fun and mindbending, and for me, they can be split in three categories:

- Engineering - figuring out how to get the text blocks in the right place and right order
- R&D - bashing your head against the wall until you figure out the new mechanic you've never seen before

I very much liked the first two elements, and third one was more of a miss than a hit. [H1][i]Baba, bagarre ? [/i][/h1] [i]On pourrait se poser la question de qui est Baba.
L'abréviation d'un célèbre dessert, d'un camp romain ou d'un joueur d'Arma 3 ?
Pour paraphraser le premier ministre du moment : eh bien non. Baba, au-delà d'être un genre de petit mouton, c'est vous.
Mais parfois pas. 
Et en réalité vous serez et ferez beaucoup de choses.[/i]

[b]Baba is you est un jeu de puzzle diablement bien pensé, et probablement un des plus difficiles qui existent, avec un maître mot : penser hors du cadre.[/b]

Sans rentrer dans la mécanique exacte du puzzle, Baba a un schéma global assez classique : plusieurs mondes, dans lesquels on a plusieurs mini niveaux, et qui nécessitent d'en accomplir un nombre minimum avant de passer au prochain monde, et ainsi de suite.
[b]Et, ces niveaux, peuvent plus ou moins tous se résoudre en moins d'une minute, mais trouver leur solution peut en prendre quelques dizaines. Ceci essentiellement dû au fait de comprendre les règles du niveau et surtout, en changer pour atteindre son objectif. Puisque vous aurez la possibilité de changer les règles du jeu, c’est même une condition pour progresser. [/b]
Concept un peu unique (jamais vu ailleurs pour ma part) et sur lequel je vais rester volontairement un peu cryptique.

Ce que je peux dire en revanche, c'est qu'[b]il y a trois catégories d'énigmes[/b] :[list][*]Celles où la solution vous apparaîtra quasi évidente y compris dans des niveaux "élevés".
[*]Celles où vous sentez ce qu'il faut faire, mais où il vous manque un petit truc pour vous débloquer (comme le fameux mot/nom que vous avez sur le bout de la langue mais qui ne sort pas).
[*]Celles où vous n'aurez aucune idée de quoi faire, et où vous allez tourner en rond malgré des tests. Et vous ferez comme à peu près toute personne normalement constituée et frustrée, c’est-à-dire, aller voir sur l’Internet 2.0.[/list]

J'avoue d’ailleurs ne pas avoir réussi à choisir quelle était des deux dernières catégories la plus frustrante. 
Les énigmes évidentes ou difficiles ne seront probablement pas les mêmes entre vous et un autre, dépendant plutôt de comment vous êtes "câblés".

Ce qu'il faut surtout avoir en tête en démarrant Baba, pour avoir dû regarder moi-même quelques solution, c’est qu'au moins un bon 3/4 de vos points de blocage ont une solution évidente et applicable en 30 secondes... mais que vous n'avez juste même pas envisagé.
La raison ? Très certainement, qu'en étant tellement focalisé sur une logique/voie, elle a inconsciemment occulté toutes les autres, dont celle qui permet d'aller au bout.

Il reste cependant quelques énigmes un peu plus alambiquées, qui mettront vos neurones à rude épreuve.

[b] La conclusion de Baba, c'est qu'il encourage à tester, à trouver de nouvelles voies, modifier les règles et penser hors du cadre. Très bon jeu mais probablement pas à la portée de tout le monde.[/b]

186676226.review:
This is an amazing puzzle game, and the best kind.  It's a very simple idea that allows for incredibly interesting and continually novel interactions among the parts of the game.  The art is simple but cute and each time I solve a puzzle I feel a genuine sense of achievement.  Unlike most puzzle games, the more difficult puzzles aren't made by simply putting more moving parts into the machine and making things complicated, but instead are increasingly clever applications of existing methods and occasional additions of new methods.

The core idea is that each level has rules that are set by simple sentences built out of blocks of text.  BABA IS YOU, for instance, means that the player controls Baba.  If you push any part of that sentence out of the way, it breaks, and you no longer control Baba.  Depending on how you push the text, that could mean you've failed the round or it could mean that now you've got control of a key, or a rock, or something else entirely.  The player has to figure out how to use, or more often change, existing rules in order to reach the winning condition.  It's surprisingly fun and challenging.

184987180.review:
I've 100-percented this game and now it's time to review it.

Firstly, it is a masterpiece of programming artistry with a genius concept. The music and visuals are pretty good too. That's about all the good I have to say about it.

The audience for this consists of masochists, people with above average IQs, people who want to waste their time, and puzzle enjoyers who don't care about getting anywhere even close to completing games. That last one is a problem for achievement hunters like me and one of the reasons I don't like it.

This game is absurdly difficult. It legitimately makes Souls-likes look like a baby smashing two rocks together. The reason it's so difficult is because completing levels requires zero skill, only brainpower. Lots and lots of brainpower. There's even an undo button.

It relies on your lack of knowledge of its convoluted, unintuitive, and downright questionable mechanics and interactions to be difficult. If all the mechanics were clearly shown, then it would cease to be difficult for the majority of the levels, which is how it should've been designed. Instead, it throws you headfirst into levels requiring mechanics that would maybe take you years to discover.

The store page gives you the impression that the game allows you to beat levels in creative and open-ended ways but this is not the case at all. Level solutions are very rigid and specific, especially later in the game. There is no room for player expression or creativity. Beating the game requires extreme logic and sometimes extreme irrationality.

This causes it to leave the territory of "a fun game which is therefore not a waste of time" and cross into "a massive waste of time so much so that almost anything else would be a better use of it". Seriously, most people could probably get their PhD in the time that it would take them to 100-percent this game without guides or hints, which is why the vast majority of people use them. It's such a waste of time that people in multiple comment sections of solution videos that I found have said it took them WEEKS just to solve a SINGLE LEVEL. You're better off spending your time on problems that actually matter and help humanity progress instead of playing this. You'd also be more fulfilled, but that bar is very low when it comes to this game.

On my quest to 100-percent it and subsequently write this review, I oftentimes opened it, thought something along the lines of "I really don't want to deal with having to solve this puzzle or follow a guide right now", and then closed it immediately after. It's genuinely mentally exhausting. In some sessions of playing, I just stared at the screen for hours while attempting to think of the solution so, in a sense, it's more of a waste of time than watching paint dry because at least that takes far less time and you can maybe paint some more afterward.

At one point, I came up with the bright idea to take notes to help me find the solution faster, but I quickly realized that it would simply be writing down every possible combination of words that actually does something and then doing a ton of trial and error. At that point, the game stopped being a puzzle and started being a brute force decryption simulator, which felt like bashing my head against a wall. I read another review where someone said that the game felt like his job, which I think was programming, and if he wanted to feel like he's doing more work then he would just actually go do more work. This is the perfect description of it: a video game version of manual tedious mathematics and logic problems such as stoichiometry, long division, and any factorization of large numbers or equations.

In most sessions before I started looking up guides, I made zero progress. Eventually I started setting a time limit for myself on each level which when expired, I would look up a guide or the solution. This actually increased my enjoyment of the game but it still sucked because following the convoluted solutions required a notable amount of mental energy. Any game that requires the players to restrict or limit themselves beyond how it already is to enjoy it more is poorly designed. The designer's entire job is to make the game enjoyable, not to make it into one that requires the player to do certain things for it to work as it's supposed to.

Also, any game that requires the players to refer to an external source to enjoy it more is poorly designed. This is definitely a game that would've been much better with a "hint" or "show solution" button or both that pops up after a certain amount of time has been spent in a level. Actually, would that have made the game better or would it have emphasized how poorly designed it truly is? It could've been designed in a way to better prepare the players to beat the game on their own and then it wouldn't feel like it needs those buttons. This is something I call "negative handholding".

Speaking of the developer, he has to be a super sadist, a master troll, a power-tripping egotist, an extremely dense genius, or a combination of any of those. Here is some evidence to support that claim.
- Levels often have a solution that seems clear or correct but actually isn't due to it being explicitly prevented in the rules. It has A LOT of these "bait solutions" and they only serve to make the game unenjoyable.
- When watching solution videos, I discovered that some were outdated due to the fact that the levels were updated to be more difficult.
- A majority of the game feels like you're at the whims of a kid in control of the rules for a pretend play battle. There's almost a constant "that just doesn't work because I said so" and "that attack didn't work because I blocked it".
- Most of the levels made by people besides the developer are some of the easiest in the game.
- Lastly, the evidence to show that the developer might just be a dense genius and not someone who revels in knowing that they're causing others to suffer, which is most likely, is that he could have had a case of what I call "developer blindness", which occurs when a developer and/or the consultants become so familiar with the product that they forget what it's like to be someone experiencing it for the first time, causing them to neglect developing it in a way that would make it enjoyable for anyone besides themselves.

To conclude, Baba Is You is an extremely difficult puzzle game that is a masterpiece in programming with quirky audio and visuals which ends up being an unrewarding and unenjoyable waste of time most of the time due to extreme design oversights. I only kept playing because I'm a completionist who wanted to conquer it, beat it into submission, and not let it win because it's utter bullcrap. It truly is a test, in puzzle game form, of how much bullcrap someone can tolerate before stopping.

这款游戏说实话一开始上手时是非常让人惊喜的，推箱子加语义解密的玩法非常有创意，在最初几个大章节总体上还算是颇具可玩性。然而越往后这款游戏就有越来越多的缺点暴露。
（1）解密思路严重缺乏引导性：很多关卡的解法完全就是突然空降的，没一丁点前置关卡循序渐进地引导玩家思路
（2）过度依赖信息差增加难度：这一点和问题（1）是一对孪生兄弟，很多关卡之所以难，能卡玩家很久乃至根本无从下手，从根本上就是因为设计者和玩家存在信息差，有些机制完全是作者的程序设计、结算顺序等导致的，而这些特性玩家既不可能从逻辑推理中获得，游戏本身也没有提供任何合理、可观、公平的线索。说实话这一点真的让这游戏后期有些关卡的体验完全是毁灭性的，玩家抓破脑袋解不出来，一搜答案，完全没有那种豁然开朗、柳暗花明的妙处，只给人一种“就这啊？”的无语感。
（3）限制唯一解但是充斥着干扰项：越玩到后面越能感觉到这游戏的作者就是故意要限制唯一解（尽管有些关卡没成功），这游戏的底层机制原本充满无限的可能性，但是作者就是喜欢按着玩家头教你玩游戏，很多小细节明显能看出是作者为了限制多解故意在关卡里放了一些看起来很突兀的东西，而这些用于限制多解的语句或是墙体反而会在关卡上手一开始时严重干扰乃至误导玩家的思路，玩家顺着走下去发现这条路正好是作者不希望你走的、被堵死的思路。除此之外这游戏的地图本身也充斥着和正确答案没有任何关系的多余元素，这里一棵树，那里一堵墙，那边又有一条可以走的路，这些东西存在的意义就是混淆玩家的观察和思维。当你发现这些观察半天的元素没有任何存在价值，或是某条思路被作者简单粗暴的堵死，那种挫败感真的非常强烈。PLUS：搜答案的过程中发现很多关都被作者修改甚至重做过，可见作者对于限制玩家思路可谓是非常执着，你就得按我设计的玩游戏，我不允许你在我的游戏里另辟蹊径收获别样的快乐。
综上所述，这游戏玩到后面可玩性、趣味性直线走低，玩一关就是纯在揣测作者的思路而不是发挥自己的想象力。你可能反对说解密游戏就该是这样，我只能说与其玩这样的关卡我不如去学习。

184603078.review:
Most puzzle games demand you to think 'outside the box'. In Baba is You, there is no box. This game will present to you so many simple yet impossible levels, you'll swear your game is bugged. But there is always some ingenious, big-brain solution, hiding in plain sight.

If you look at the comment section of any Baba is You solution video, you will find no shortage of angry commenters. They will claim, "That's not fair! The game never taught me I could do that!" even though it has. In a moment of weakness, they blamed the game and not themselves.

Here's the thing - you cannot expect to try multiple permutations of one-dimensional solutions and expect to make progress. Baba is You will not give you the satisfaction of beating it for free. You will have to push the rules to its limit. You will have to create infinite combos, clip through walls, and build complex machinery using nothing but four words and a rock.

Now, that's not to say looking up hints or solutions is bad. Unless you're like me, who has zero respect for their time, it's perfectly reasonable to say no to another hour of banging your head against the wall for one level. But when you do decide to wave the white flag, don't go telling the game dev off for making a game that finally respects people's intelligence, just because you feel it disrespects your stupidity.

If you ever happen to be part of the 2.6% of people that beat all 200+ levels in this game, know that it will be a lonely achievement. Your parents, who have never touched a video game in their life, they wouldn't understand. Your old high school buddies, who only contact you when they need something, they wouldn't understand. Your Steam friends, they've never even heard of Baba is You, they wouldn't understand.

But know, just know, that I will understand.

The mechanics of the game are mostly intuitive, and each time a new mechanic is introduced, it is done in either a clear and understandable manner or through a purposeful challenge of reflexion.

The levels drastically increase in difficulty after the first few chapters, and become severely complexe and time consuming to solve, landing quite far outside the range of casual puzzles.
To me personally, there came a point where that amount of complexity and time investment overtook the amount of fun and satisfaction gained from completing levels, essentially causing a feeling of being burned out from the game. Be aware that if you pick up this game and intend to finish it, it is a long and arduous endeavor.

The visual aesthetics of the game are clean, recognizable, and of good quality.

[b]Baba Is You[/b] is overall a good quality, well-thought-out, very challenging, and very unique puzzle game from [b]Hempuli Oy[/b].
